title: Introduce granular commit-fence and utilization resolver
author: Samir Patel
release_notes: Introduces a commit-fence mechanism and utilization resolver to reduce overcommit and improve headroom accuracy for Dedicated fleets; adds new telemetry surfaces and a gradual rollout plan.
description: Context and motivation: Dedicated pools occasionally overcommit during rapid demand spikes because the autoscaler decisions and reservation bookkeeping operate on slightly mismatched windows. This PR introduces a lightweight commit-fence abstraction that decouples commit intent from immediate reservation application and a UtilizationResolver that correlates sampled utilization histograms to conservative commit windows so we can smooth oversubscription while preserving throughput guarantees. Goals: 1) reduce failed reservation rollbacks and noisy headroom oscillation; 2) provide observability into commit intent vs applied reservations; 3) enable gradual canary rollout controlled by config flags. Changes: high-level summary of commits: Add commit-fence controller and API surface; Implement UtilizationResolver module and unit tests; Instrument reservation service to emit commit_intent, commit_apply, and commit_reject events; Add metrics: reserved_intent_count, commit_lag_ms, util_resolver_score; Extend autoscaler to consult UtilizationResolver when proposing new reservations; Add feature flag and canary rollout scaffolding; Migration: database tag added to reservation records (migration script included). Files changed (high-level): serving/reservations/commit_fence.go (core controller and state machine), serving/reservations/commit_fence_test.go (unit tests + deterministic fake clock), serving/autoscaler/resolve_utilization.go (resolver and mapping logic), serving/autoscaler/resolve_utilization_test.go (statistical test harness), ops/migrations/20251102_add_commit_tag.sql (simple column add and backfill), observability/metrics.yaml (new metric declarations), console/ui/reservations_overview.tsx (small UI element showing intent vs applied counts), helm/redwood-values.yaml (feature flag default off), docs/operational/commit_fence.md (operator-facing runbook), examples/canary/commit-fence-config.yaml (canary config). Review conversation summary: Priya: "Can you clarify failure modes when commit_apply fails during partial node outage?" Author: "If commit_apply fails we record a commit_reject with reason and the fence enters a retryable backoff; autoscaler is designed to treat commit_intent as advisory until commit_apply success — added doc section and expanded test to cover transient node outage." Ethan: "The util_resolver scoring thresholds look tight for some traffic shapes; can we expose tuning via config map?" Author: "Exposed tunables as helm values and added a runtime config with sane defaults; added calibration notes to the resolver test harness so infra can derive thresholds from their own traffic snapshots." Marta: "Add end-to-end integration test or blue-green canary?" Author: "Added a small e2e scenario in the bench harness that validates no more than 1% of intents are rejected under synthetic ramp; canary recipe included in examples." Review status: Priya approved after one follow-up patch; Ethan requested a small change to a metric label which was fixed; Marta gave thumbs-up on canary recipe. CI: initial lint failure (naming on metric) fixed in follow-up commit, full test matrix passed (unit, integration, flake detection), bench job ran in canary mode and reported stable util score. Rollout plan and risk mitigation: Default feature flag OFF in main release; staging rollout to 10% of dedicated fleets for two weeks, observe commit_reject and commit_lag metrics, then gradual 25/50/100; automatic rollback if commit_reject rate > 0.5% sustained over 5 minutes. Operational runbook: docs/operational/commit_fence.md includes steps to enable, metric dashboards to watch, and a quick rollback path. Performance notes: small CPU overhead on reservation coordinator (~2-3% on 95th percentile under synthetic load) and negligible memory impact; latency impact limited to commit path where commit_apply remains asynchronous and does not block serving surface. Testing: unit coverage added for state transitions, integration tests for autoscaler interaction, bench harness validating stability under ramp. Backwards compatibility and migrations: DB migration adds commit_tag column with backfill script; system supports zero-downtime migration and flag gating to prevent early use. Additional context and related work: complements previous headroom smoothing efforts (see ENG-2980) and aims to reduce oscillations captured by the fleet telemetry team. Merge outcome: PR was squashed and merged to main on 2025-11-09 (merge commit c3f9d2b).
notes: Canary config, migration script, and docs included. Ops must run migration during maintenance window for fleets with >100 nodes.
